title: This Clam Lives 168 Years With a 3-Foot Neck
subject: geoduck

scenes.text: This animal barely moves, yet it outlives almost everything.
It's the geoduck, say gooey-duck, a giant clam from the Pacific Northwest.
It digs about three feet down into the sediment, one foot a year.
From down there, a siphon up to three feet long reaches the water above to feed and breathe.
It weighs only about seven pounds, but the oldest one recorded was 168 years old.
Born before the lightbulb, and still sitting in the mud.

description:
A giant clam that barely moves can live 168 years.
The geoduck buries itself about three feet deep and reaches the surface with a siphon up to three feet long.
How old are you compared to the oldest geoduck?
first_comment: Would you eat something that lived through two centuries? Or is that too old?
